subject: COVID-19 Response
overview: The panel discussed Medford's local public health response to COVID-19, focusing on emergency measures and food security initiatives. Participants also reviewed technical barriers to online grocery shopping for SNAP recipients and the health risks facing the state's incarcerated population.

items.title: Medford COVID-19 Public Health Response
items.summary: Councilor Zac Bears discussed Medford's early implementation of school closures and business restrictions, directing residents to the city website for emergency orders.

items.title: Economic Support and Housing Policy
items.summary: The discussion addressed the need for direct income support and state legislation to freeze the economy, including an eviction and foreclosure moratorium.

items.title: Food Security and Mutual Aid Networks
items.summary: Councilor Bears highlighted Medford's Food Security Task Force, grab-and-go meal sites for seniors and families, and the installation of micro-pantries.

items.title: SNAP Benefits and Online Grocery Delivery
items.summary: Becca Miller explained that federal USDA regulations and technical limitations currently prevent SNAP recipients in Massachusetts from using benefits for online grocery delivery.

items.title: Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) and Food Resources
items.summary: Participants discussed the HIP program, which allows for fresh produce delivery with in-person EBT processing, and provided the Project Bread hotline for application assistance.

items.title: Prison Conditions and COVID-19 Safety
items.summary: Caroline Bays reported on the lack of social distancing, inadequate cleaning, and insufficient medical staffing within state correctional facilities during the pandemic.

items.title: Decarceration and Solitary Confinement Reform
items.summary: The panel discussed efforts by District Attorneys to release high-risk or pre-trial individuals and reviewed the excessive use of solitary confinement in Massachusetts prisons.
